did_you_know.text: Did you know? In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest made a covenant with five commanders of hundreds, including Azariah son of Jeroham and Ishmael son of Jehohanan, to work together to enthrone the king’s son.
Did you know? For this plan, the Levites were gathered in Jerusalem from all the cities of Judah, together with the heads of Israel’s ancestral families.
Did you know? The covenant was made in the house of God, and it was declared that the king’s son would reign, as the LORD had promised concerning the descendants of David.

Did you know? Jehoiada divided those coming on duty into three groups: one stationed at the Gate of Sur, one at the royal palace, and one at the Foundation Gate; the rest of the people stood in the courtyards of the house of the LORD.

Did you know? Jehoiada did not dismiss the divisions of the priests and Levites; instead, he joined those coming on duty with those going off duty so that the guard would continue without interruption.
Did you know? Jehoiada gave the commanders of hundreds the spears, shields, and bucklers that had belonged to King David and had been kept in the house of God.
Did you know? At Joash’s coronation, both the crown and the testimony were placed on him. Then Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and the people shouted, “Long live the king!”
Did you know? Jehoiada ordered that Athaliah not be killed in the house of the LORD, but be taken outside its precincts; she was killed near the entrance of the Horse Gate at the royal palace.
Did you know? After making a covenant to be the LORD’s people, the people demolished the temple of Baal, smashed its altars and images, and killed Mattan, the priest of Baal.

Did you know? Jehoiada restored the worship in the house of the LORD to its proper order: the priests and Levites offered burnt offerings as prescribed in the Law of Moses, accompanied by joy and singing according to the arrangement established by David.
